bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in src/range.c (range_num_to_a): while converting numeric ranges to an array the function can write an 8-byte value past the end of the allocated array (out-of-bounds write). This corrupts heap memory and can lead to crashes or potential arbitrary code execution when handling certain numeric ranges (e.g., mixes of integers and floats).
bug_description.normalized: The staged input bytes begin with `0xff 0x20` and then place a top-level splat on the inclusive range text `-9223723685475807..-9223723685475807.1`. On the reproduced run, mruby still lexes the begin endpoint as an integer literal and the end endpoint as a float literal, constructs an inclusive `Range`, and forces `Range#to_a` through the `*`. In vulnerable `src/range.c`, the integer begin is first cast to `mrb_float` and the array capacity is computed from floating-point endpoint subtraction, but the inclusive loop also uses that imprecise float as its induction variable. On the reproduced 64-bit/double build, those conversions collapse the large endpoints enough that `a <= b` stays true while `a += 1.0` does not advance to a new representable value, so the loop keeps issuing `ptr[i++] = ...` writes after the small destination chosen by `(mrb_int)(b - a) + 1` is exhausted. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting 8-byte heap-buffer-overflow at `src/range.c:403`.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed path that consumes attacker-controlled Ruby source bytes and materializes vulnerability-relevant data. The lexer turns the begin literal text from the staged PoC into the integer AST node later used as the range's begin endpoint.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` bytes begin `ff 20 2a 2d 39 32...`; after that prefix, `parser_yylex` reads the begin literal text `9223723685475807` from the `*-9223723685475807..-9223723685475807.1` portion and creates the integer node used as the range's begin endpoint.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The inclusive integer-begin/float-end conversion loop performs another 8-byte store through `ptr[i++]` after the destination chosen by `mrb_ary_new_capa` has already been exhausted.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by commit `f4de2059603088ff488480072f13322cd3670de2`. Vulnerable code converts the integer begin endpoint to `mrb_float` and then reuses that imprecise float for both capacity derivation and loop induction. The patch keeps `a` as `mrb_int` and rewrites the loop as an integer-controlled `for`, eliminating the precision-loss mismatch between reserved length and write count.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker controls both numeric endpoint literals in the Ruby source. This first materialization step creates the begin value that later flows into the mixed integer/float range conversion logic and participates in the lossy float cast at the root cause.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific admitted continuation. The witness is accepted as Ruby range syntax when the parser reduces the two attacker-controlled numeric operands around `..` using the inclusive-range grammar arm. That proves the file was parsed as Ruby source and advanced into the exact mixed-endpoint range path, not merely to the generic CLI entry point.

fine_trace.note: After the staged file's `0xff 0x20` prefix, the lexer reads the attacker-controlled begin token `9223723685475807` from the `*-9223723685475807..-9223723685475807.1` portion and materializes it as the integer literal node that will become the range's begin endpoint.
The unary minus in the PoC wraps the integer literal node from step 1, turning the begin endpoint into the negative integer `-9223723685475807` used by the range expression.

The lexer then reads the attacker-controlled end token `9223723685475807.1` after `..` in that same trailing source fragment and materializes it as the float literal node for the range's end endpoint.
The second unary minus turns the float literal from step 3 into the negative float end value `-9223723685475807.1`.
The parser reduces the two negative numeric operands around `..` into an inclusive range AST node, preserving the mixed integer-begin/float-end shape that selects the vulnerable branch later.
The `*` byte at offset 2 in the staged witness wraps that range expression in a splat node, making array conversion reachable instead of leaving the range as an unused literal.

fine_trace.code: mrb_value v = mrb_range_new(mrb, regs[a], regs[a+1], FALSE);
fine_trace.note: When the compiled script runs, the inclusive range opcode creates the `Range` object with the negative integer begin and negative float end produced by the parser.
The compiled splat expression from step 6 is executed, so mruby must convert the just-created range object into an array through `mrb_ary_splat`.
Because the splatted object is a `Range`, `mrb_ary_splat` dispatches `to_a`, and `Range#to_a` immediately delegates numeric ranges to the vulnerable C helper `__num_to_a`.

Inside the integer-begin/float-end branch, the begin endpoint is lossy-cast from `mrb_int` to `mrb_float`. For the PoC's large magnitude on this 64-bit/double build, that conversion collapses the integer begin to an imprecise floating value that will also be used as the loop variable.
The end endpoint is loaded as `mrb_float` as well, so both range bounds are now compared and sized in floating-point rather than in exact integer arithmetic.

The destination extent is derived from the rounded float difference `(mrb_int)(b - a) + 1`, then `ptr = RARRAY_PTR(ary)` exposes that storage. For the witness, this reserves only a small array even though the subsequent loop will not make matching progress.

Because the range is inclusive, the code enters the `while (a <= b)` loop instead of the exclusive branch. With the PoC's rounded large endpoints, `a <= b` holds and later `a += 1.0` may fail to move `a` to a new representable float, so the loop's write count is no longer bounded by the capacity computed in step 12.

Sink. The loop issues another 8-byte store through `ptr[i++]` after the small array reserved in step 12 has been exhausted. The saved crash trace reports `WRITE of size 8` and identifies this exact line, `src/range.c:403:22`, as the heap-buffer-overflow site.

format.contract: The saved witness is narrower than generic Ruby source: the staged file begins with bytes `ff 20` and then contains the fragment `*-9223723685475807..-9223723685475807.1`. The source-grounded requirement established here is that mruby admits that fragment as a top-level splat of the inclusive mixed-endpoint range, yielding an integer begin, a float end, and a `Range#to_a` call through the splat on this vulnerable build.
